**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Sugarcane (long, narrow grass-like leaves in a field setting)
- **Affected parts**: Leaves — particularly the midrib/central vein region
- **Key features observed**:
  - The central young leaves display a prominent **yellowish/pale tan coloration along the midrib** (central vein), while the surrounding leaf blade remains relatively green
  - Older leaves in the background are completely straw-yellow/dried — indicating disease progression
  - The yellowing appears to radiate from the midrib outward

**Differential reasoning:**

| Disease | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Yellow_Leaf** | Strong match — midrib yellowing is the hallmark symptom; older leaves progressing to full straw-color |
| Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv | Would show fine parallel chlorotic streaks throughout the blade, not focused on midrib |
| Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus | Mosaic/irregular green-yellow patches across blade, not midrib-centered |
| Leaf_Scald | Would show water-soaked pencil-line margins, more marginal than midrib |
| Pokkah_Boeng | Would show distorted/twisted young spindle leaves |
| Brown_Spot | Would show brown oval/circular lesions |
| Yellow_Spot | Would show yellow oval spots, not streaking |

The **midrib-centered yellowing** with adjacent green leaf tissue on younger leaves, progressing to fully yellow/dried older leaves in the background, is the classic presentation of **Yellow Leaf** disease (caused by Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus, ScYLV).

This midrib-centered yellowing pattern is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Yellow Leaf disease (ScYLV), distinguishing it from mosaic viruses (which show blade-wide mosaic patterns) and leaf scald (which shows marginal streaks)."}
